title: Filesystem layout
description: Where an instance keeps its files, with what permissions, and which account owns them. Every default here is overridable per host; the defaults exist so that a request with no overrides still produces a complete, defensible plan.

paths.description: Every kind of file an instance writes, keyed by what the file is for. A data path and a log path are the minimum any engine has: an instance whose logs go nowhere is one nobody can operate afterwards.

propertyNames.description: The purpose of the path, as the plan labels it. Which purposes exist is the engine's business, not the core's.

default.description: An absolute path, which may reference the engine and instance placeholders.

mode.description: Directory permissions, quoted so that 0700 survives YAML parsing intact.

min_free.description: Free space the mount carrying this path must have. This is a block threshold, so it has to be a number someone will defend in a review.

prefer_separate_from.description: The other purposes this path would rather not share a mount with, named as they are keyed here. Sharing is supported and only warns, because two paths on one filesystem compete for the same free space and the same queue, and lose each other's failure isolation.

create_if_missing.description: Whether Basewright may create the account. False means a host without it is refused rather than modified.

shell.description: A login shell for a database service account is an unnecessary way in.

group.description: Absent means a group named after the account.

size.description: A quantity of bytes with an explicit unit. Decimal and binary units are both accepted and mean what they say.
